paras: Did you know that FDPS raised a record breaking $28 000 at this year’s Colour Fun Run? All the money donated is going towards the Stephanie Alexander Kitchen Garden Program, one of the school’s most crucial and favourable programs for FDPS students.

The Stephanie Alexander Kitchen Garden Program (SAKG) is a program our school has newly introduced and has been run in the garden and on Thursdays in the staffroom. This beloved program is designed to bring kids and cooking together with a focus on the importance of healthy nutritious food.

news.title: Is Taekwondo an art or A Sport?
paras: And then… silence, and then someone from the crowd shouted… “Is Taekwondo a sport or is it a performing arts?” Well we are here to answer that question! Did you know that Taekwondo is Korean? In Korean, chung and hung mean blue and red.

They use these colours to represent a competitor at a competition. You wear protective gear in that colour on your stomach. Otherwise, you wear your own white gear. According to sources such as The Korea Herald and Kiddle, Taekwondo is a form of performing art, because you don’t just fight, you learn a pattern.

news.title: On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1
paras: India swung for the moon with Chandrayaan-1, its first deep space mission. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor.

Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. news.title: Digital scents could add a new dimension to virtual worlds
paras: That’s the promise of an AI-assisted device that can transmit smells over the internet. So far, it works on only a small number of scents, including orange, beer and cake, but its creators hope the system will ultimately recreate more smells.

The scent of a pine forest or the aroma of coffee, for example, could then add a new dimension to virtual worlds and long-distance communication. Although it is now routine to communicate sight, sound and even touch sensations electronically, smell is “still a very undeveloped sense”, says Chunyu Yang at the Ohio State University.
